docs.title: Multi-Tenancy Guide
docs.text:
Isolate documents by namespace within a single table for multi-tenant applications.

Namespaces scope vector-store operations inside a database. To select an application virtual cluster through the connection URL, see Virtual-cluster connections.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Multi-tenancy lets multiple tenants share the same vector store table while keeping their data completely isolated. Each tenant's documents are invisible to other tenants during search, retrieval, and deletion.

CockroachDB suits this pattern because its C-SPANN vector indexes support prefix columns. With the namespace as the index's prefix column, the namespace filter is applied at the index level, not as a post-filter.

docs.title: 1. Create a table with a namespace column
docs.text:
from langchain_cockroachdb import CockroachDBEngine

engine = CockroachDBEngine.from_connection_string(
    "cockroachdb://root@localhost:26257/defaultdb?sslmode=disable"
)

await engine.ainit_vectorstore_table(
    table_name="documents",
    vector_dimension=1536,
    namespace_column="namespace",  # opt-in: adds the namespace column
)

docs.title: 2. Create per-tenant vector stores
docs.text:
from langchain_cockroachdb import AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore
from langchain_openai import OpenAIEmbeddings

embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings()

# Tenant A's view
store_a = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine=engine,
    embeddings=embeddings,
    collection_name="documents",
    namespace="tenant-a",
)

# Tenant B's view
store_b = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine=engine,
    embeddings=embeddings,
    collection_name="documents",
    namespace="tenant-b",
)

docs.title: 3. Operations are automatically scoped
docs.text:
# Each tenant only sees their own documents
await store_a.aadd_texts(["Tenant A's document"])
await store_b.aadd_texts(["Tenant B's document"])

results_a = await store_a.asimilarity_search("document", k=10)
# Returns only: ["Tenant A's document"]

results_b = await store_b.asimilarity_search("document", k=10)
# Returns only: ["Tenant B's document"]

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When namespace is set on a vector store instance:

  • Insert: Documents are tagged with the namespace value
  • Search: A WHERE namespace = '...' filter is automatically injected
  • Delete: Only documents in the namespace can be deleted
  • Get by IDs: Only returns documents belonging to the namespace

When namespace is None (the default), no filtering is applied and all documents are visible. This preserves full backward compatibility.

docs.title: Search isolation
docs.text:
await store_a.aadd_texts(["AI research paper"], ids=[id_1])
await store_b.aadd_texts(["AI product docs"], ids=[id_2])

# Tenant A only finds their documents
results = await store_a.asimilarity_search("AI")
assert len(results) == 1
assert results[0].page_content == "AI research paper"

docs.title: Delete isolation
docs.text:
# Deleting in tenant A doesn't affect tenant B
await store_a.adelete([id_1])

results_b = await store_b.asimilarity_search("AI")
assert len(results_b) == 1  # Tenant B's doc is untouched

docs.title: Get by IDs isolation
docs.text:
# Tenant A can't see tenant B's documents even by ID
docs = await store_a.aget_by_ids([id_2])
assert len(docs) == 0  # Not visible across namespaces

docs.title: Document ID rules
docs.text:
Document IDs must be unique across all namespaces. A write that reuses another namespace's id raises ValueError before anything is written. The library generates random UUIDs for ids, so this only matters for ids you supply.

# Tenant A adds document with id_1
await store_a.aadd_texts(["Document A"], ids=[id_1])

# Tenant B tries to add a document with the same id -- rejected
try:
    await store_b.aadd_texts(["Document B"], ids=[id_1])
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)  # Duplicate id in another namespace

docs.title: Admin Access (No Namespace)
docs.text:
Create a store without a namespace to see all documents across all tenants. This is the unscoped, admin-style view, and it is intended. The admin store can update rows in any namespace:

admin_store = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine=engine,
    embeddings=embeddings,
    collection_name="documents",
    # no namespace parameter -- sees everything
)

all_docs = await admin_store.asimilarity_search("AI", k=100)
# Returns documents from all tenants

# Admin store can also update or delete documents in any namespace
await admin_store.adelete([id_from_tenant_a])

docs.title: Performance: C-SPANN Prefix Columns
docs.text:
For best performance with multi-tenancy, create a vector index with the namespace as a prefix column:

from langchain_cockroachdb.indexes import CSPANNIndex

index = CSPANNIndex(name="documents_ns_vec_idx")
await store_a.aapply_vector_index(index, prefix_columns=["namespace"])

This creates CREATE VECTOR INDEX ... ON documents (namespace, embedding vector_cosine_ops), which partitions the index by namespace. A search within a namespace takes its nearest vectors from that namespace's part of the index, with or without a metadata filter. With a filter, the store applies it to those vectors, and when they may have left matches out it runs the exact search, which returns only the namespace's rows but can scan the whole table to find them (see Filtered Search). The namespace must be the index's only prefix column, and the table needs the plain index on the namespace column that ainit_vectorstore_table creates. An index on the embedding alone cannot serve a namespaced store's searches, since CockroachDB counts namespace = ... as a filter.

docs.title: Metadata Filtering with Namespaces
docs.text:
Namespace filtering composes with metadata filters:

results = await store_a.asimilarity_search(
    "machine learning",
    k=5,
    filter={"category": "research"},
)
# Filters by namespace="tenant-a" AND metadata.category="research"

docs.title: When to Use Namespaces vs Separate Tables
docs.text:
Approach Use when Namespace column Many tenants, shared schema, need cross-tenant admin queries Separate tables (collection_name) Few tenants, different schemas, strict physical isolation

For most multi-tenant SaaS applications, the namespace approach is recommended because it avoids table proliferation and works naturally with CockroachDB's prefix column indexing.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Vector Indexes - Create prefix-column indexes for multi-tenant performance
  • Vector Store - Core vector store operations

docs.title: Retries and Resilience
docs.text: CockroachDB runs every transaction at SERIALIZABLE isolation and keeps serving through node restarts, drains and region failures. Clients are expected to retry a few kinds of errors, and langchain-cockroachdb does it on every database call: the vector store, chat history, both LangGraph checkpointers and the long-term memory store.

docs.title: What gets retried
docs.text:
SQLSTATE Meaning Why a retry is safe 40001 Serialization failure ("restart transaction") The transaction did not commit 40003 Result is ambiguous Every write the library issues is idempotent 08xxx Connection exceptions, including CockroachDB sqlproxy's 08C00 Idempotent writes, and the pool replaces the connection 57P01 Node draining or shutting down Idempotent writes 58C00 Range unavailable (CockroachDB) Usually clears once leases move 58C01 Connection failure between CockroachDB nodes Usually clears once leases move 53300 Too many connections Connection slots free up

Errors that arrive without a SQLSTATE, which is how the driver reports most connection failures, are retried when SQLAlchemy marks the connection invalidated or when the message matches a known connection-loss phrase. CockroachDB's uncategorized codes (XXUUU, XX000) are matched against known phrases too, for example "read tcp ...: i/o timeout" that can follow a canceled session. Failed logins and SSL or configuration mistakes are never retried, even though the driver reports them without a code, so a bad password does not trip an account lockout.

Everything else is raised right away, including statement timeouts (57014) and XXA00 (the data was committed but a schema change failed).

docs.title: Configuring retries
docs.text:
Set a RetryPolicy once on the engine. The vector store and chat history inherit it; each can override it, and the checkpointers take their own.

from langchain_cockroachdb import (
    AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore,
    CockroachDBChatMessageHistory,
    CockroachDBEngine,
    RetryPolicy,
)

engine = CockroachDBEngine.from_connection_string(
    "cockroachdb://root@localhost:26257/defaultdb?sslmode=disable",
    retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=8, max_backoff=5.0),
)
store = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(engine, embeddings, "documents")  # inherits
history = CockroachDBChatMessageHistory("session-1", engine=engine)  # inherits
fast_store = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine, embeddings, "documents", retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=2)
)
Field Default What it does max_attempts 5 Total attempts, including the first initial_backoff 0.1 Seconds before the first retry max_backoff 10.0 Cap for any delay backoff_multiplier 2.0 Growth between delays jitter 0.5 Share of each delay that is randomized (0 turns it off) retryable_sqlstates RETRYABLE_SQLSTATES Codes to retry retryable_sqlstate_classes {"08"} Two-character classes to retry uncategorized_sqlstates {"XXUUU", "XX000"} Codes too generic to decide on; message phrases decide transient_messages TRANSIENT_MESSAGES Phrases that mark a code-less error as transient non_transient_messages NON_TRANSIENT_MESSAGES Phrases that rule a retry out retry_on None Your own predicate, replacing the rules above attempt_timeout None Seconds before a hung query or write is abandoned and retried ddl_attempt_timeout None The same guard, for each schema change

Policies are plain data, so they can come from configuration files or environment variables:

policy = RetryPolicy(**{"max_attempts": 6, "retryable_sqlstates": ["40001", "40003", "57P01"]})

The older retry_max_attempts, retry_initial_backoff, retry_max_backoff, retry_backoff_multiplier and retry_jitter arguments still work as shorthand.

TTL changes get one more rule. CockroachDB v25.4 refuses to change a table's TTL settings while another schema change on that table runs, with SQLSTATE 0A000. Several processes running checkpointer enable_ttl or disable_ttl, or store setup() with a TTL configuration or disable_ttl, at once can hit it, and so can a store setup() that meets another process's migration backfilling the table. These TTL statements are idempotent, so they retry that error (schema_change_policy), even if your retry_on would refuse it. The other schema change can take far longer than a transient error takes to clear, such as a column backfill or a vector index build, so this error has a budget of its own: each TTL statement retries it for up to SCHEMA_CHANGE_BUSY_SECONDS (600, ten minutes) of wall time from the first such error, as long as the store's setup() waits for another process's migration (SCHEMA_CHANGE_SETTLE_SECONDS). A store setup() can wait one such budget for each table whose TTL it changes, on top of that wait. The pauses grow as your backoff does, from the default initial backoff if yours has none, at least doubling, up to SCHEMA_CHANGE_BUSY_MAX_BACKOFF seconds (3). Other errors keep your policy's attempts and backoff, counted apart from it, and a RetryPolicy subclass keeps its is_retryable and delay overrides for them (not overrides of run or arun). max_attempts=1 turns every retry off. The code and phrase are SCHEMA_CHANGE_BUSY_SQLSTATE and SCHEMA_CHANGE_BUSY_MESSAGES, and is_schema_change_busy() checks an error.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text:
A 40001 means the transaction did not commit. After a 40003 or a dropped connection it may have. Retrying is only safe when running the work twice has the same effect as running it once, and every write the library makes is built that way: vector inserts are UPSERTs, deletes are deletes, chat messages carry ids chosen before the first attempt and are written with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, checkpoints are UPSERTs, and schema changes use IF [NOT] EXISTS.

For your own code, async_retry_with_backoff and sync_retry_with_backoff use the same rules. If the work is not idempotent, retry serialization failures only:

from langchain_cockroachdb import async_retry_with_backoff, get_sqlstate


@async_retry_with_backoff(retry_on=lambda error: get_sqlstate(error) == "40001")
async def transfer(conn):
    ...

docs.title: Riding through a regional failover
docs.text:
While leases move after a node or region failure, statements can wait several seconds. If your application sets a statement_timeout, those statements fail with 57014. Add the code to the policy, and cut off attempts that hang:

from langchain_cockroachdb import RETRYABLE_SQLSTATES, RetryPolicy

failover = RetryPolicy(
    max_attempts=8,
    max_backoff=5.0,
    retryable_sqlstates=RETRYABLE_SQLSTATES | {"57014"},
    attempt_timeout=10,
)

Statement timeouts are not retried by default because they also fire for genuinely slow queries, and retrying those multiplies load on the queries that are already slow.

On Linux, also add tcp_user_timeout=10000 to the connection URL. attempt_timeout starts only once a connection is checked out, so this is what keeps a pool's pre-ping on a connection to a lost node from hanging for minutes.

docs.title: Cutting off hung attempts
docs.text:
attempt_timeout gives each attempt a deadline. When it passes, the library shuts down the connection's socket, so the stuck call fails as a lost connection and the normal retry runs on a fresh connection. It starts once a connection is checked out, so it does not cover getting a connection: connect_timeout bounds opening a new one, and a pool_pre_ping on a pooled connection whose peer went silent is only cut short by tcp_user_timeout (see Connection settings). This works even when the server ignores cancel requests, which CockroachDB can do for a COMMIT while a range it wrote to has lost quorum, and it ends reads stalled by a network partition long before the operating system's TCP timeouts would.

It is off by default. Good starting points are 10 to 30 seconds for interactive paths and 60 to 120 seconds for batch work. Schema changes use ddl_attempt_timeout, also off by default, which bounds each schema change: one statement in the vector store, chat history and engine setup, one migration step or one TTL statement in the checkpointers, and one migration step or one schema statement (vectors table, vector index, TTL) in the store. Building an index on a large table can legitimately take minutes.

docs.title: Checkpointers: use a connection pool
docs.text:
A single connection cannot recover once it drops, so the savers do not retry a dead single connection. Give them a pool, which replaces broken connections and enables concurrent operations:

from psycopg.rows import dict_row
from psycopg_pool import ConnectionPool

from langchain_cockroachdb import CockroachDBSaver, RetryPolicy

with ConnectionPool(
    "postgresql://root@localhost:26257/defaultdb?sslmode=disable",
    kwargs={"autocommit": True, "row_factory": dict_row},
    open=True,
) as pool:
    checkpointer = CockroachDBSaver(pool, retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=8))
    checkpointer.setup()  # safe to run from several processes at once

A saver on a pool runs operations concurrently, each on its own pooled connection, so one saver can serve many agents, threads or tasks. A saver on a single connection (including pipeline=True) runs operations one at a time, so long-running services should use a pool. A shared pooled saver runs as many operations at once as the pool has connections, so set max_size for the number of agents you expect to run at the same time. psycopg_pool's default max_size equals min_size, which defaults to 4. When every connection is busy, an operation waits up to the pool's timeout and then raises PoolTimeout, which is not retried.

Pooled savers retry when psycopg reports the connection broken, even when the error text is unfamiliar. This includes retries over TLS: on CockroachDB Cloud a dropped connection reads "SSL error: unexpected eof while reading" (OpenSSL 3), which is now recognized and retried.

put with channel blobs, put_writes with several writes, and delete_thread send BEGIN, their statements and COMMIT as one batch, so each write is saved completely or not at all, even when the caller is cancelled or fails partway. A write still takes one round trip, and CockroachDB can still retry it on the server. On a single connection that the caller also uses, a write made inside a transaction the caller opened joins it as a savepoint, so the caller's commit or rollback decides.

from_conn_string accepts retry_policy, connect_timeout, prepare_threshold and connect_kwargs (for example {"application_name": "my-service"}).

docs.title: Connection settings
docs.text:
• connect_timeout defaults to 10 seconds. A value in the URL or connect_args wins; pass connect_timeout=None to leave it unset.
  • pool_pre_ping (on by default) checks a pooled connection before use, so connections that died while idle are replaced without an error. A pre-ping on a connection whose peer went silent can wait for the operating system to give up, so pair it with tcp_user_timeout below.
  • TCP keepalives detect dead peers on idle connections, for example ?keepalives_idle=30&keepalives_interval=10&keepalives_count=3. On Linux, tcp_user_timeout (in milliseconds, for example ?tcp_user_timeout=10000) cuts off a pre-ping or query on a connection whose peer went silent, without waiting for the OS retransmission timeout (which can be 15 minutes).
  • gssencmode defaults to disable for new connections. CockroachDB has no GSS encryption, and this also avoids a Kerberos lookup that can crash forked workers on macOS. Values in the URL or connect_args override it. If you build a connection pool yourself (not through the engine's from_connection_string), add gssencmode=disable to the pool's conninfo or kwargs on macOS with prefork servers.

docs.title: Sync and async
docs.text:
Async methods run on your event loop. Sync methods run their database work on one background event loop, so they are safe from any number of threads and from inside a running event loop. Use one style per engine; the engine logs a warning if it sees both at the same time. Engines that use the built-in background loop are also safe across os.fork(): a child process gets a fresh pool and loop.

An engine built with loop= (CockroachDBEngine(engine, loop=...) or CockroachDBEngine.from_engine(engine, loop=...)) sends its sync calls, and async calls from other event loops, to that loop. Keep the loop running in its thread while the engine is in use. If the loop is closed, is not running, or stops while a call waits on it, the call raises RuntimeError instead of waiting forever. A loop that is not running gets about a second to start, or to start again, before calls give up. When a call gives up after its work started, the work may or may not have taken effect. The library's writes are safe to retry (see Idempotency). The loop's thread does not survive os.fork(), so in a child process such an engine raises RuntimeError too, and so does a new engine built there on a loop that was running in the parent. Build a new engine in the child, with a loop started in the child, or without loop=.

docs.title: Watching retries
docs.text:
Each retry logs one WARNING on the langchain_cockroachdb.retry logger:

WARNING langchain_cockroachdb.retry: Retrying insert into public.resilience_1ceb80 after SerializationFailure (SQLSTATE 40001): restart transaction: demo fault 40001 (attempt 1 of 6 failed, next try in 0.10s)

and one more when it gives up. Raise that logger's level to hide them, or route them to your metrics.

Waits for another schema change log less often. A TTL change that meets another schema change on its table logs one WARNING on its first retry, then at most one every SCHEMA_CHANGE_PROGRESS_SECONDS (60), with how long it has waited, and one when it gives up:

WARNING langchain_cockroachdb.retry: Retrying store TTL setup after FeatureNotSupported (SQLSTATE 0A000): cannot modify TTL settings while another schema change on the table is being processed: another schema change on the table is still running (attempt 1 failed, 0s of up to 600s waited, next try in 0.09s)

A store setup() that waits for another process's migration logs on the store's logger: an INFO line when it starts, a WARNING once it has waited SCHEMA_CHANGE_QUIET_SECONDS (30), then one every minute with how long it has waited and what it still waits for (the columns, or schema change jobs that SHOW JOBS shows on the table), and an INFO line when it ends. The WARNING reads:

WARNING langchain_cockroachdb.store.store: setup() has waited 31s for another process to apply migration 2 to public.store: its columns are not public yet, and SHOW JOBS shows 1 schema change job on the table. Check SHOW JOBS for the schema change job. setup() waits up to 600 seconds in all.

When no job applies the migration and that setup() applies the migration itself, it logs that at INFO.

docs.title: Trying it
docs.text: examples/resilience.py makes CockroachDB raise real 40001, 40003 and 57P01 errors and kills pooled connections while the vector store, chat history and checkpointer keep working.

docs.title: Vector Indexes Guide
docs.text: Optimize query performance with CockroachDB's C-SPANN vector indexes.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
CockroachDB uses C-SPANN (CockroachDB SPANN - Scalable Partitioned Approximate Nearest Neighbors) for vector indexing. This algorithm is optimized for distributed databases and provides:

  • Real-time indexing (no rebuild needed)
  • Automatic sharding and rebalancing
  • Fresh results (queries see latest data)
  • Distributed query execution

docs.title: When to Use Indexes
docs.text:
Use indexes when: - ✅ Dataset > 10,000 vectors - ✅ Query latency is critical - ✅ Frequent searches on same dataset - ✅ Multi-tenant with prefix columns

Skip indexes when: - ❌ Dataset < 1,000 vectors - ❌ Mostly writes, few reads - ❌ Data changes constantly - ❌ Acceptable to scan all vectors

docs.title: Create Index
docs.text:
from langchain_cockroachdb import CSPANNIndex

# Create with defaults
index = CSPANNIndex()
await vectorstore.aapply_vector_index(index)

This creates: 

CREATE VECTOR INDEX IF NOT EXISTS documents_embedding_vector_idx
ON public.documents (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

docs.title: Specify Distance Strategy
docs.text:
from langchain_cockroachdb import CSPANNIndex, DistanceStrategy

# Cosine similarity (default)
index = CSPANNIndex(distance_strategy=DistanceStrategy.COSINE)
await vectorstore.aapply_vector_index(index)

# Euclidean distance (L2)
index = CSPANNIndex(distance_strategy=DistanceStrategy.EUCLIDEAN)
await vectorstore.aapply_vector_index(index)

# Inner product
index = CSPANNIndex(distance_strategy=DistanceStrategy.INNER_PRODUCT)
await vectorstore.aapply_vector_index(index)

docs.title: Partition Sizes
docs.text:
Control how vectors are partitioned:

index = CSPANNIndex(
    distance_strategy=DistanceStrategy.COSINE,
    min_partition_size=10,    # Minimum vectors per partition
    max_partition_size=100,   # Maximum vectors per partition
)
await vectorstore.aapply_vector_index(index)

Guidelines: - Smaller partitions = higher accuracy, slower queries - Larger partitions = faster queries, lower accuracy - Default (None) = CockroachDB chooses optimal size

docs.title: Custom Index Name
docs.text:
index = CSPANNIndex(name="my_custom_index_name")
await vectorstore.aapply_vector_index(index)

docs.title: Prefix Columns
docs.text:
An index can have prefix columns before its vector column. They come only from prefix_columns, never from the order of the table's columns:

# The table was created with namespace_column="namespace"
index = CSPANNIndex()
await vectorstore.aapply_vector_index(index, prefix_columns=["namespace"])

This creates: 

CREATE VECTOR INDEX IF NOT EXISTS documents_embedding_vector_idx
ON public.documents (namespace, embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CockroachDB uses such an index only for a search that constrains every prefix column to a value, with = or IN. A store created with namespace="tenant-a" adds namespace = 'tenant-a' to each of its searches, so an index whose only prefix column is the namespace serves them, with or without a metadata filter. A store without a namespace constrains no column, so it cannot use an index with prefix columns. The store never constrains a column other than the namespace.

A key in filter is a filter on the JSON metadata column, not a prefix column, even when it has the name of a column.

Benefits: - Each tenant's vectors are stored together in the index - A search reads only its own tenant's part of the index

docs.title: Filtered Search
docs.text:
CockroachDB uses a vector index only when every filter of the search matches the index's prefix columns. A metadata filter never does. So when the filter sits next to ORDER BY distance LIMIT k, CockroachDB scans the table and ranks every row that passes.

When the table has a usable index (see below), a search with a filter works in steps instead:

  1. It takes the nearest rows from the index, with no filter: twice k plus one, and at least 41, which costs the index about the same as fewer (on a 20,000-row table, a window of 41 read about 10% more rows than a window of 9, in the same time). For a namespaced store, the namespace is the index's prefix column, so the index reads only that namespace.
  2. It applies the filter to those rows and keeps the k nearest that pass. Steps 1 and 2 are one statement.
  3. When fewer than k rows pass, matches may lie beyond the window, so the store runs the exact search: the statement every filtered search ran before 0.6.0, which filters before it ranks. When no row passes, it always does. When some do, it skips the exact search only if the window held every row of the table or namespace, since the short result is then the whole answer.

A filter that most rows near the query pass is served by the index alone, in one statement. A selective filter often needs the exact search as well, which costs the scan it always did, plus the short indexed read before it. The exact search returns only the store's namespace, but its plan can scan the whole table to find those rows.

A result that comes from the window is approximate, as every index search is: the index can miss a near neighbor, and the beam size sets how often (see Beam Size). Before 0.6.0, filtered searches scanned and were always exact.

A usable index:

  • is on the store's embedding column;
  • has the operator class of the store's distance strategy (see Index Opclasses);
  • has no prefix column for a store without a namespace, and the namespace column as its only prefix column for a namespaced store.

A namespaced store also needs the primary key or another index to lead with the namespace column, so that counting the namespace's rows does not scan the table. ainit_vectorstore_table creates that index with the namespace column. A table without one keeps the exact search.

The store reads the table's indexes with SHOW CREATE TABLE on its first filtered search. The engine keeps the answer for every store with the same table, embedding column, distance strategy and namespace column, so an application that builds a store per request, one per tenant for example, reads it once per table, not once per request. It is read again once VECTOR_INDEX_REFRESH_SECONDS (60) have passed, so an index that another process creates is used within a minute, and right after an index is applied or dropped through any store on the engine. Without a filter, or without a usable index, a search runs the same single statement as before.

This covers similarity_search and its variants, max marginal relevance search and the vector leg of hybrid search, in the sync and async stores. In MMR search the candidate pool, fetch_k, takes the place of k. In hybrid search, so does its pool: fetch_k, or max(4 * k, 20) without it.

docs.title: Beam Size
docs.text:
The beam size sets how much of the index a search explores. CockroachDB's default, the vector_search_beam_size session setting, is 32. Pass query_options to change it for one search:

from langchain_cockroachdb import CSPANNQueryOptions

# A larger beam: more accurate, slower
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search(
    "query", k=10, query_options=CSPANNQueryOptions(beam_size=64)
)

# A smaller beam: faster, less accurate
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search(
    "query", k=10, query_options=CSPANNQueryOptions(beam_size=16)
)

The store sets it with SET LOCAL in the search's own transaction, so it never stays on a pooled connection. The MMR methods take query_options= too.

Guidelines: - Start with the default, 32 - If results miss near neighbors, try 64, then 128 - If latency matters more than recall, try 16 - Check recall against an exact search on a sample of real queries

docs.title: Drop Index
docs.text:
await vectorstore.adrop_vector_index()

Or by name: 

DROP INDEX index_name;

docs.title: Check Index Status
docs.text:
async with engine.engine.connect() as conn:
    from sqlalchemy import text
    result = await conn.execute(
        text("""
            SELECT indexname, indexdef 
            FROM pg_indexes 
            WHERE tablename = 'documents'
        """)
    )
    for row in result:
        print(f"Index: {row[0]}")
        print(f"Definition: {row[1]}")

docs.title: Rebuild Index
docs.text:
Indexes are maintained automatically, but if needed:

# Drop and recreate
await vectorstore.adrop_vector_index()
index = CSPANNIndex()
await vectorstore.aapply_vector_index(index)

docs.title: Small Dataset (1,000 vectors)
docs.text:
Configuration Query Latency Notes No index 4-5ms Fast enough, index not needed With index 5-10ms Index overhead > benefit

Recommendation: Skip index for < 10K vectors

docs.title: Medium Dataset (50,000 vectors)
docs.text:
Configuration Query Latency Notes No index 50-200ms Sequential scan slow With index 10-30ms 5-10x faster Index, beam below the default 32 5-15ms Fast but less accurate Index, beam above the default 32 15-40ms More accurate

Recommendation: Create index, tune beam size for workload

docs.title: Large Dataset (1M+ vectors)
docs.text:
Configuration Query Latency Notes No index 5-30s Unusable With index 20-100ms Essential Index + partitions 10-50ms Tuned partitions help

Recommendation: Always use index, tune partitions and beam

docs.title: Index Opclasses
docs.text:
The index uses the operator class of its distance strategy. The vector store sets this automatically when you call aapply_vector_index:

Distance Strategy Opclass Operator COSINE vector_cosine_ops <=> EUCLIDEAN (L2) vector_l2_ops <-> INNER_PRODUCT vector_ip_ops <#>

Upgrading from 0.3.x

Indexes created by earlier versions for COSINE or INNER_PRODUCT are vector_l2_ops and are not used by those searches. Drop them with await vectorstore.adrop_vector_index() and apply again. aapply_vector_index logs a warning when it finds a mismatched opclass, different prefix columns, or a partition size other than one you set. Applying the same index again logs nothing.

docs.title: 1. Create the Index Before Writes Start
docs.text:
# Create the table, then the index while the table is empty
await engine.ainit_vectorstore_table("documents", vector_dimension=1536)
await vectorstore.aapply_vector_index(CSPANNIndex())

# Then write
await vectorstore.aadd_texts(texts)

Building an index on a table that already holds data starts a backfill, and CockroachDB blocks writes to the table until the backfill ends. This is a known limitation of vector indexes. On a table that takes writes all the time, create the index before the writes start. To index a table that already holds data, choose a time when its writes can pause.

docs.title: 2. Use the Namespace as the Prefix Column for Multi-Tenancy
docs.text:
# One store per tenant, on a table created with namespace_column="namespace"
store = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine=engine,
    embeddings=embeddings,
    collection_name="documents",
    namespace="tenant-123",
)
await store.aapply_vector_index(CSPANNIndex(), prefix_columns=["namespace"])

# The index reads only tenant-123's vectors; the filter applies to them
results = await store.asimilarity_search("query", k=10, filter={"category": "news"})

A key in filter, such as "tenant_id", filters the JSON metadata. It never uses an index prefix.

docs.title: 3. Monitor and Tune Beam Size
docs.text:
# Start with the default, 32
# Monitor query latency and recall
# If too slow: try 16
# If results miss near neighbors: try 64, then 128

docs.title: 4. Consider Workload Balance
docs.text: Workload Strategy Read-heavy Create the index right away Write-heavy Create the index on the empty table, before writes start: building it on a table that holds data blocks writes until the backfill ends Balanced Create the index early, and monitor performance

docs.title: 5. Index Before Production
docs.text:
# Development: test without index first
# Staging: create index, benchmark
# Production: deploy with index

docs.title: Index Not Being Used
docs.text:
Check query plan: 

EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM documents 
ORDER BY embedding <=> '[...]' LIMIT 10;

If index not used: - Check distance operator matches index opclass - Check that the query constrains every prefix column to a value; a metadata filter alone never uses the index (see Filtered Search) - Verify table statistics are up to date - Use CockroachDB v25.4 or later, the oldest version this library supports

docs.title: Slow Index Creation
docs.text:
Large datasets take time: 

import time

start = time.time()
await vectorstore.aapply_vector_index(index)
elapsed = time.time() - start
print(f"Index created in {elapsed:.1f}s")

Typical times: - 10K vectors: 1-5s - 100K vectors: 10-30s - 1M vectors: 1-5 minutes

docs.title: Accuracy Issues
docs.text:
Increase the beam size above the default of 32: 

results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search(
    "query", k=10, query_options=CSPANNQueryOptions(beam_size=64)
)

Or adjust partition sizes: 

index = CSPANNIndex(
    min_partition_size=5,   # Smaller = more accurate
    max_partition_size=50,  # Smaller = more accurate
)

docs.text:

  • API Reference - Full index API

docs.title: Vector Store Guide
docs.text: Complete guide to using the CockroachDB vector store.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore provides a high-performance interface for storing and searching vector embeddings in CockroachDB.

docs.title: Initialization
docs.text:
from langchain_cockroachdb import AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore, CockroachDBEngine
from langchain_openai import OpenAIEmbeddings

# Create engine
engine = CockroachDBEngine.from_connection_string(
    "cockroachdb://user:pass@host:26257/db"
)

# Initialize table
await engine.ainit_vectorstore_table(
    table_name="documents",
    vector_dimension=1536,
)

# Create vector store
vectorstore = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine=engine,
    embeddings=OpenAIEmbeddings(),
    collection_name="documents",
)

docs.title: From Text
docs.text:
# Simple text
texts = [
    "CockroachDB is a distributed database",
    "LangChain simplifies LLM applications",
]
ids = await vectorstore.aadd_texts(texts)
print(f"Added {len(ids)} documents")

docs.title: With Metadata
docs.text:
texts = ["Doc 1", "Doc 2", "Doc 3"]
metadatas = [
    {"source": "web", "category": "tech", "year": 2024},
    {"source": "pdf", "category": "science", "year": 2023},
    {"source": "api", "category": "tech", "year": 2024},
]

ids = await vectorstore.aadd_texts(texts, metadatas=metadatas)

docs.title: From Documents
docs.text:
from langchain_core.documents import Document

documents = [
    Document(
        page_content="Content here",
        metadata={"source": "file.txt", "page": 1}
    ),
    Document(
        page_content="More content",
        metadata={"source": "file.txt", "page": 2}
    ),
]

ids = await vectorstore.aadd_documents(documents)

docs.title: With Custom IDs
docs.text:
import uuid

custom_ids = [str(uuid.uuid4()) for _ in range(len(texts))]
ids = await vectorstore.aadd_texts(texts, ids=custom_ids)

docs.title: Batch Size Control
docs.text:
# Override default batch size at runtime
ids = await vectorstore.aadd_texts(
    large_text_list,
    batch_size=500  # Larger batches for throughput
)

docs.title: Similarity Search
docs.text:
# Basic search
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search(
    "distributed databases",
    k=5
)

for doc in results:
    print(f"Content: {doc.page_content}")
    print(f"Metadata: {doc.metadata}")

docs.title: With Scores
docs.text:
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search_with_score(
    "distributed databases",
    k=5
)

for doc, score in results:
    print(f"Score: {score:.4f}")
    print(f"Content: {doc.page_content}")

docs.title: By Vector
docs.text:
# Search with your own vector
embedding = embeddings.embed_query("my query")
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search_by_vector(
    embedding,
    k=5
)

docs.title: With Relevance Scores
docs.text:
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search_with_relevance_scores(
    "query",
    k=5,
    score_threshold=0.7  # Only return scores above threshold
)

docs.title: Supported Operators
docs.text:
Operator Meaning Example $eq Equals (default) {"status": {"$eq": "active"}} or {"status": "active"} $ne Not equals {"status": {"$ne": "archived"}} $lt Less than {"year": {"$lt": 2024}} $lte Less than or equal {"year": {"$lte": 2023}} $gt Greater than {"score": {"$gt": 0.5}} $gte Greater than or equal {"score": {"$gte": 0.5}} $between Between two values {"year": {"$between": [2020, 2024]}} $in In list {"category": {"$in": ["tech", "science"]}} $nin Not in list {"status": {"$nin": ["draft", "deleted"]}} $exists Field exists {"optional_field": {"$exists": true}} $like SQL LIKE (case-sensitive) {"title": {"$like": "%Python%"}} $ilike SQL ILIKE (case-insensitive) {"title": {"$ilike": "%python%"}} $and Logical AND {"$and": [{"year": 2024}, {"status": "active"}]} $or Logical OR {"$or": [{"category": "tech"}, {"category": "science"}]} $not Logical NOT {"$not": {"status": "archived"}}

All values are passed as bound parameters, so apostrophes and other characters need no escaping. Range operators like $lt, $lte, $gt, $gte compare numbers numerically and strings as text.

docs.title: Basic Filters
docs.text:
# Equality
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search(
    "tech content",
    k=5,
    filter={"category": "tech"}
)

# Multiple conditions (implicit AND)
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search(
    "recent tech",
    k=5,
    filter={"category": "tech", "year": 2024}
)

docs.title: Comparison Operators
docs.text:
# Greater than
filter={"year": {"$gt": 2020}}

# Greater than or equal
filter={"year": {"$gte": 2020}}

# Less than
filter={"score": {"$lt": 0.9}}

# Less than or equal
filter={"score": {"$lte": 0.9}}

# Not equal
filter={"status": {"$ne": "archived"}}

docs.title: IN and NOT IN
docs.text:
# IN operator
filter={"category": {"$in": ["tech", "science", "engineering"]}}

# NOT IN operator
filter={"status": {"$nin": ["draft", "archived"]}}

docs.title: Logical Operators
docs.text:
# AND (explicit)
filter={
    "$and": [
        {"category": "tech"},
        {"year": {"$gte": 2023}}
    ]
}

# OR
filter={
    "$or": [
        {"category": "tech"},
        {"category": "science"}
    ]
}

# Complex nested
filter={
    "$and": [
        {"year": {"$gte": 2023}},
        {
            "$or": [
                {"category": "tech"},
                {"category": "science"}
            ]
        }
    ]
}

docs.title: Filter Examples
docs.text:
# Recent tech or science documents
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search(
    "innovation",
    k=10,
    filter={
        "$and": [
            {"year": {"$gte": 2023}},
            {"category": {"$in": ["tech", "science"]}}
        ]
    }
)

# High-quality documents from specific sources
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search(
    "research",
    k=10,
    filter={
        "$and": [
            {"source": {"$in": ["arxiv", "nature", "ieee"]}},
            {"quality_score": {"$gte": 0.8}}
        ]
    }
)

docs.title: Update Documents
docs.text:
# Re-add with same ID to update
await vectorstore.aadd_texts(
    ["Updated content"],
    ids=["existing-id"]
)

docs.title: Delete by IDs
docs.text:
ids_to_delete = ["id1", "id2", "id3"]
await vectorstore.adelete(ids=ids_to_delete)

docs.title: Delete All
docs.text:
# Delete all documents in collection
await vectorstore.adelete()

docs.title: As Retriever
docs.text:
# Convert to LangChain retriever
retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(
    search_type="similarity",
    search_kwargs={"k": 5}
)

# Use in chains
from langchain.chains import RetrievalQA
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

qa = RetrievalQA.from_chain_type(
    llm=ChatOpenAI(),
    chain_type="stuff",
    retriever=retriever,
)

answer = await qa.ainvoke("What is CockroachDB?")

docs.title: MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance)
docs.text:
# Diverse results (less similar to each other)
retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(
    search_type="mmr",
    search_kwargs={
        "k": 10,
        "fetch_k": 50,  # Fetch more candidates
        "lambda_mult": 0.5  # Balance relevance vs diversity
    }
)

# Or directly
results = await vectorstore.amax_marginal_relevance_search(
    "query",
    k=10,
    fetch_k=50,
    lambda_mult=0.5
)

docs.title: Similarity Score Threshold
docs.text:
# Only return highly relevant results
retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(
    search_type="similarity_score_threshold",
    search_kwargs={
        "k": 10,
        "score_threshold": 0.8
    }
)

docs.title: Distance Strategies
docs.text:
Choose distance metric based on your embeddings:

from langchain_cockroachdb import DistanceStrategy

# Cosine similarity (default, normalized vectors)
vectorstore = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine=engine,
    embeddings=embeddings,
    collection_name="docs",
    distance_strategy=DistanceStrategy.COSINE
)

# Euclidean distance (L2)
vectorstore = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine=engine,
    embeddings=embeddings,
    collection_name="docs",
    distance_strategy=DistanceStrategy.EUCLIDEAN
)

# Inner product
vectorstore = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine=engine,
    embeddings=embeddings,
    collection_name="docs",
    distance_strategy=DistanceStrategy.INNER_PRODUCT
)

docs.title: Which to Use?
docs.text: Distance Strategy Best For Normalized? Cosine Most embeddings (OpenAI, Anthropic) Yes Euclidean (L2) Spatial data, distances matter No Inner Product Pre-normalized vectors, speed priority Yes

docs.title: Drop Table
docs.text: await vectorstore.adrop_table()

docs.title: Check if Table Exists
docs.text:
async with engine.engine.connect() as conn:
    from sqlalchemy import text
    result = await conn.execute(
        text("""
            SELECT EXISTS (
                SELECT FROM information_schema.tables 
                WHERE table_name = 'documents'
            )
        """)
    )
    exists = result.scalar()

docs.title: 1. Use Appropriate Batch Sizes
docs.text:
# Smaller embeddings
vectorstore = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine=engine,
    embeddings=embeddings,
    collection_name="docs",
    batch_size=500  # < 512 dims
)

# Larger embeddings
vectorstore = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine=engine,
    embeddings=embeddings,
    collection_name="docs",
    batch_size=100  # > 1024 dims
)

docs.title: 2. Create Indexes

from langchain_cockroachdb import CSPANNIndex

# Create vector index for faster queries
index = CSPANNIndex()
await vectorstore.aapply_vector_index(index)

See Vector Indexes Guide for details.

    connection_string,
    pool_size=20,      # More connections for concurrency
    max_overflow=40,

docs.title: 4. Filter Early
docs.text:
# Good: Filter reduces candidates before vector search
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search(
    "query",
    k=10,
    filter={"category": "tech"}  # Narrows search space
)

# Less efficient: No filter means searching all vectors
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search(
    "query",
    k=10
)
# Then filter results in Python

docs.title: Multi-Tenant Isolation
docs.text:
# Store tenant_id in metadata
await vectorstore.aadd_texts(
    texts,
    metadatas=[{"tenant_id": "tenant-123"}] * len(texts)
)

# Query with tenant filter
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search(
    "query",
    k=5,
    filter={"tenant_id": "tenant-123"}
)

docs.title: Versioning Documents
docs.text:
# Include version in metadata
await vectorstore.aadd_texts(
    ["Document content"],
    metadatas=[{"doc_id": "abc123", "version": 2}]
)

# Query latest version
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search(
    "query",
    k=5,
    filter={"version": {"$gte": 2}}

docs.title: Source Attribution
docs.text:
# Track sources
metadatas = [
    {
        "source": "https://example.com/page1",
        "title": "Page Title",
        "author": "John Doe",
        "date": "2024-01-15"
    }
]

await vectorstore.aadd_texts(texts, metadatas=metadatas)

# Search and cite sources
results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search_with_score(
    "query", k=3
)

for doc, score in results:
    print(f"Source: {doc.metadata['source']}")
    print(f"Relevance: {score:.2f}")

docs.title: Multi-Tenancy (Namespaces)
docs.text:
Isolate documents by tenant within a single table:

# Create table with namespace column (opt-in)
await engine.ainit_vectorstore_table(
    table_name="documents",
    vector_dimension=1536,
    namespace_column="namespace",
)

# Per-tenant stores
store_a = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine=engine, embeddings=embeddings,
    collection_name="documents", namespace="tenant-a",
)
store_b = AsyncCockroachDBVectorStore(
    engine=engine, embeddings=embeddings,
    collection_name="documents", namespace="tenant-b",
)

# All operations (search, delete, get_by_ids) are scoped to the namespace
await store_a.aadd_texts(["Tenant A doc"])
results = await store_a.asimilarity_search("doc")  # Only tenant A's docs

See the Multi-Tenancy Guide for the full guide including C-SPANN prefix column indexing.

docs.text:
import asyncio

try:
    results = await vectorstore.asimilarity_search("query", k=5)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Search failed: {e}")
    # Retry logic is automatic, but you can catch final failure

docs.title: Virtual-cluster connections
docs.text: A virtual cluster is a database target selected by the connection URL. Point each client (the engine, chat history, and the checkpointers) at the SQL URL for the virtual cluster you want, and the library preserves that routing. How you select a virtual cluster depends on whether it is managed or self-hosted.

docs.title: Managed virtual clusters (Cockroach Continuum)
docs.text:
A Cockroach Continuum deployment is a host cluster, a Mission Critical cluster with virtualization enabled, currently in preview. Each virtual cluster on the host has its own SQL connection string, its own network security configuration, and its own SQL users. Generate a virtual cluster's connection string from the Cloud Console's Connect dialog or with the ccloud CLI, and use it as is:

postgresql://app:PASSWORD@vc-endpoint.aws-us-east-2.cockroachlabs.cloud:26257/agents?sslmode=verify-full

Do not add a -ccluster option to a Continuum connection string; the generated string already reaches its virtual cluster. A host cluster's console URL is a management address, not a SQL connection string. Keep the supplied hostname, port, database, and TLS parameters, including sslrootcert when needed, and do not assume a virtual cluster is named main or build its connection string from the host's identifier. An application connected to a virtual cluster cannot see or reach the host or any other virtual cluster in the workspace. See Virtual clusters on a Continuum host. This integration does not provision virtual clusters.

docs.title: Self-hosted virtual clusters
docs.text:
On a self-hosted deployment with cluster virtualization enabled, select the application virtual cluster with the connection URL's options parameter:

postgresql://app:PASSWORD@HOST:26257/agents?sslmode=verify-full&options=-ccluster%3Dmain

Here main selects the application virtual cluster, while agents selects a database inside it. Create the database and grant the application user access before connecting. Application workloads belong on the application virtual cluster; the system virtual cluster is for administration and physical cluster replication (PCR). CockroachDB documents this routing syntax in Work with Virtual Clusters. The self-hosted virtualization limitations currently allow one system virtual cluster and one application virtual cluster per physical cluster, so testing two self-hosted application virtual clusters requires two physical clusters, or one virtualized cluster that compares the main and system virtual clusters. The engine, chat history and saver examples below accept the supplied SQL URL either way.

docs.title: Engines and chat history
docs.text:
Store the complete connection URL in COCKROACHDB_URL:

import os

from langchain_cockroachdb import CockroachDBChatMessageHistory, CockroachDBEngine

engine = CockroachDBEngine.from_connection_string(os.environ["COCKROACHDB_URL"])
history = CockroachDBChatMessageHistory("conversation-1", engine=engine)

The vector store uses the same engine. Chat history can also take the URL directly through connection_string=. A shared engine reuses one connection pool; close it when the application shuts down.

The library normalizes postgresql://, cockroachdb://, and cockroachdb+psycopg:// to the SQLAlchemy CockroachDB dialect with psycopg 3. It preserves the rest of the URL, including virtual-cluster routing, TLS parameters, and other connection settings.

docs.title: Checkpointers
docs.text:
Both saver factories accept the same URL:

import os

from langchain_cockroachdb import AsyncCockroachDBSaver, CockroachDBSaver

with CockroachDBSaver.from_conn_string(os.environ["COCKROACHDB_URL"]) as saver:
    saver.setup()


async def setup_async() -> None:
    async with AsyncCockroachDBSaver.from_conn_string(os.environ["COCKROACHDB_URL"]) as saver:
        await saver.setup()

The factories normalize the URL to postgresql:// for psycopg and preserve its query parameters. For concurrent agents, use a pooled checkpointer and pass a postgresql:// URL directly to psycopg_pool. Pool constructors are provided by psycopg and do not normalize cockroachdb:// URLs.

docs.title: Long-term memory store
docs.text:
CockroachDBStore and AsyncCockroachDBStore accept the same URL through from_conn_string, including the pool_config path, which builds the pool from the normalized URL. Point them at the same virtual cluster:

import os

from langchain_cockroachdb.store import CockroachDBStore

with CockroachDBStore.from_conn_string(os.environ["COCKROACHDB_URL"]) as store:
    store.setup()

See the long-term memory store guide for indexes, TTL and search.

docs.title: Combine connection options
docs.text:
Startup options such as the self-hosted -ccluster selector go in one options value, separated by spaces. If a connection string already carries an options value, append to it rather than replace it. For example, to select a self-hosted main cluster and set a statement timeout:

from urllib.parse import quote, urlencode

query = urlencode(
    {
        "sslmode": "verify-full",
        "options": "-ccluster=main -cstatement_timeout=5000",
    },
    quote_via=quote,
)
connection_url = f"postgresql://app:PASSWORD@HOST:26257/agents?{query}"

Encode query values once. %3D encodes = and %20 encodes a space. Use quote_via=quote when building a URL with urlencode: its default + encoding for spaces is not decoded as a space by libpq. A literal + in a query value should be encoded as %2B so both connection paths preserve it. Avoid duplicate options query parameters. Driver keyword arguments (connect_args on engines or connect_kwargs on saver factories) override URL values, so an options keyword must contain the cluster selector too.

docs.title: Routing and isolation
docs.text:
The cluster selector chooses the database target for a connection. Vector namespaces and checkpoint thread_id values scope application data inside that target. They do not authorize access or make agents communicate. Apply database privileges and application authorization for tenant access, and use distinct thread IDs for independent conversations.

URL compatibility does not establish database failover or external tool execution guarantees. See Retries and Resilience for connection-loss handling.
